newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Pasminco June qtr production falls 2.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Pasminco June qtr production falls 2.3 pct.

text.p: Base metals miner Pasminco Ltd said on Wednesday that total zinc and lead production from its mines and smelters in the June quarter was down 2.3 percent on the same quarter last year at 308,786 tonnes.
Total zinc and lead production for the 12 months to June 30 of 1.272 million tonnes was consistent with the previous year's production a 1.289 million tonnes, it said.
In its June quarter report, Pasminco said the highlight of the quarter was improved performance at the Hobart and Port Pirie smelters, where production was up eight percent on the preceding quarter.

At the Cockle Creek smelter, zinc and lead bullion production was affected by operating problems in the furnace and casting areas as the plant neared its planned four-year shutdown, expected to begin on August 3 and last four weeks.
"Approximately 5,000 tonnes of zinc will be sourced from LME warehouses in order to maintain supply to customers," Pasminco said.
At the company's Broken Hill mine ore throughput reached a record 2.7 million tonnes for the year.
Production of zinc in concentrate in the June quarter was up six percent on the previous corresponding quarter, but production of lead in concentrate was down 10 percent, due to lower lead ore grade.
Contained zinc and lead production for the year was up 12 percent and one percent respectively.
At the Eleura mine, quarterly production was down five percent on the same period last year following the suspension of production for three weeks in May after mining damage.
Recovery of zinc in concentrate was reduced due to the ore's poor metallurgical behaviour, Pasminco said.
"This situation will be remedied when alternate stoping locations become available, which is expected in September 1997," it said.
